findings.title: Rescheduled bookings pass `immediateDelete = true`, bypassing deferred cancellation and leaving stale reminder rows
findings.body: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, rescheduling a booking calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` with `immediateDelete` set to `true`. In `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (`emailReminderManager.ts` lines 213-223), when `immediateDelete` is `true` and `referenceId` is non-null, it immediately posts a cancel request to SendGrid's `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` endpoint and returns without deleting or updating the `WorkflowReminder` database record. Because rescheduling does not delete `originalRescheduledBooking` (it only marks it as `CANCELLED`), this has two consequences: (1) rescheduled bookings scheduled more than 1 hour in advance still immediately consume slots in SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellations limit instead of deferring cancellation to the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron job, and (2) the `WorkflowReminder` rows remain in the database with `cancelled: null` and `scheduled: true`, so they will be processed again if the workflow is later edited or deleted or when the cron job runs.

findings.title: `@sendgrid/client` API key is never set in `scheduleEmailReminders` cron handler
findings.body: `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` calls `sgMail.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` on line 19, but unlike `emailReminderManager.ts` (line 26), it never calls `client.setApiKey(sendgridAPIKey)` on the `@sendgrid/client` singleton. Because `@sendgrid/mail` maintains its own internal `Client` instance and does not configure the default `@sendgrid/client` instance, `await client.request({ url: "/v3/user/scheduled_sends", ... })` on line 57 (and `/v3/mail/batch` on line 188) will be sent without an API key and fail with `401 Unauthorized` whenever `emailReminderManager` has not already been loaded in the same process.

findings.title: Single failure in `remindersToCancel` loop aborts remaining cancellations and skips deleting already-cancelled rows
findings.body: In `scheduleEmailReminders.ts` lines 53-77, a single `try / catch` block wraps the entire `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop, and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls (which return lazy `PrismaPromise` objects that do not execute until awaited) are only awaited after the loop finishes via `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. If `client.request` throws for any reminder in `remindersToCancel` (for example, if its `referenceId` was already cancelled or is invalid), all subsequent reminders in the batch are skipped, and `await Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` is never reached—leaving the database rows for reminders that were already cancelled in earlier iterations of the loop undeleted so they will be retried on every future cron run. Each iteration should have its own `try / catch` (similar to `unscheduledReminders` on line 106) and `await` the database delete immediately.

findings.title: Un-awaited `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls race with cascade deletes and handler completion
findings.body: Across `workflows.tsx` (lines 212-218, 376-382, 519-525, 574-580), `handleCancelBooking.ts` (lines 485-493), `handleNewBooking.ts` (lines 966-972), and `bookings.tsx` (lines 488-494), the async functions `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called inside `.forEach(...)` without `await` or `Promise.all` (whereas previously the Prisma delete promises were awaited via `Promise.all`). In `workflows.delete` (line 220) and `workflows.update` (line 527), `ctx.prisma.workflow.deleteMany` and `ctx.prisma.workflowStep.delete` run immediately and cascade-delete the `WorkflowReminder` rows in Postgres while `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are still executing their SendGrid/Twilio API calls and subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.delete` queries, causing race conditions and allowing serverless handlers to return before the external cancellation requests finish.
